To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ectopic expression in mouse of Hox-4, a homeobox gene, causes a homeotic transformation in the occipital bone of the skull, and that the effect is restricted to regions anterior to the normal expression boundary of Hox- 4.
ectopic expression in the developing mouse embryo of a Hox gene (Hox-4.1) results in homeotic transformations in the occipital bone of the skull towards a more posterior identity.

ectopic expression in the mouse embryo of the Hox- 4.2 gene in a region anterior to its normal mesodermal expression boundary results in a homeosis of the occiput, a transformation of occipital bone morphology towards a more posterior (more caudal) phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of homeobox genes in patterning the embryonic body axis.
the molecular basis of vertebrate segmentation and with the role of Hox genes in patterning the embryonic body axes.
the molecular basis of vertebrate segmentation, a fundamental process in animal development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the posterior prevalence model, which is supported by gene disruption experiments, is not applicable to the Hox-1.1 and Hox-4 gene complexes, which are not disrupted by targeted mutagenesis.
the posterior prevalence model is supported, and that the homeotic transformation of occipital bones by Hox-4 ectopic expression is a result of the posterior prevalence model.
the Hox-2 complex is involved in patterning the axial skeleton, and the Hox-3 complex in patterning of limbs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hox-4 genes, like HOM-C genes, can transform the occipital bone of the skull towards a more posterior identity.
Hox-4 is a homeobox gene which has a homeotic effect on the occipital region of the skull.
the Hox code is not a rigidly fixed program, but is rather flexible and responsive to environmental influences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the homeotic transformation of occipital bones is not a result of the loss of Hox-4 expression, but rather a gain-of-function effect.
ectopic Hox-4 expression results in homeotic transformation of occipital bones, and that the posterior prevalence model is valid in the mouse.
the Hox- 4.2 gene is sufficient to induce a posterior phenotype in the occipital bone of the skull.
